entries.notes: One of the five DOE NSRCs; broad nanoscience infrastructure rather than a quantum-only institute. Start year is the start of operations reported by DOE. User access and available techniques should be checked on the facility site.

entries.name: National Quantum Initiative
entries.focus: Coordinates U.S. quantum research, infrastructure and workforce efforts.
entries.materials: An institutional framework for quantum science; many materials research traditions and programs predate it.
entries.notes: The initiative is not a single grant program. The agency pages below provide current center rosters; the quantum.gov overview still displays the earlier five-institute NSF roster.

sources.title: DOE: center renewal and NQI background

entries.name: Quantum Leap Challenge Institutes
entries.focus: Supports large interdisciplinary teams working on quantum computation, simulation and sensing.
entries.materials: Connects physics, materials, computing and engineering; institutes differ in how directly they study materials.
entries.status: Eight institutes listed; three new and five renewed in August 2026
entries.notes: All eight institutes in the current NSF roster are included in this directory. Q-SEnSE and RQS are NSF institutes; collaboration with NIST does not change their funding program.

entries.name: Fault Tolerant Quantum Systems, Architectures and Applications
entries.lead: Harvard University; UCLA and MIT co-lead
entries.focus: Robust hardware and software for fault-tolerant quantum systems.
entries.materials: Materials research contributes to more reliable quantum hardware.
entries.notes: Year marks the initial institute announcement.

sources.title: Fault Tolerant Quantum Systems, Architectures and Applications

entries.name: Hybrid Quantum Architectures and Networks
entries.focus: Links different kinds of quantum processors in modular networks.
entries.materials: Interfaces must connect qubits made from different physical platforms.
entries.notes: Year marks the initial institute announcement.

entries.name: Manufacturable and Resilient Superconducting Quantum Information Systems
entries.focus: Develops reproducible superconducting circuit components.
entries.materials: Connects Josephson-junction materials with semiconductor fabrication.
entries.notes: Year marks the initial institute announcement.

sources.title: Manufacturable and Resilient Superconducting Quantum Information Systems

entries.notes: Year marks the initial institute announcement.

sources.title: Physics and Engineering of Practical Quantum Error Correction

entries.name: Challenge Institute for Quantum Computation
entries.focus: Studies computing architectures and algorithms across quantum platforms.
entries.materials: Solid-state systems join atomic platforms in a shared computing research effort.

entries.name: Quantum Sensing for Biophysics and Bioengineering

entries.materials: Nanoprobes connect device materials, sensing, biology and medicine.
entries.notes: Year marks the initial institute announcement.

sources.title: Quantum Sensing for Biophysics and Bioengineering

entries.materials: Brings physics, engineering and chemistry together around sensing platforms.
entries.notes: NIST is a partner; NSF funds the QLCI. Year marks the initial institute announcement.

sources.title: Quantum Systems through Entangled Science and Engineering

entries.name: Institute for Robust Quantum Simulation
entries.focus: Builds reliable quantum simulators and methods for using them.
entries.materials: Quantum simulation provides a way to investigate complex interacting systems.
entries.notes: Year marks the initial institute announcement.

entries.name: Materials Research Science and Engineering Centers
entries.focus: Supports interdisciplinary materials research and shared experimental facilities.
entries.materials: Selected centers study quantum materials; the program covers a much wider materials landscape.
entries.notes: Predates the 2018 NQI. This directory does not list every MRSEC or imply that every MRSEC is a quantum center.

sources.title: Materials Research Science and Engineering Centers
NSF historical centers table: MRSEC began 1994

entries.name: Center for Integrated Quantum Materials
entries.lead: Harvard University, with MIT and Howard University
entries.funder: NSF Science and Technology Centers program
entries.focus: Studies quantum materials for information processing, sensing and communication.
entries.materials: Brings graphene, topological systems and diamond-based platforms into materials and device research.
entries.notes: An NSF Science and Technology Center, not a QLCI. Founded before the NQI; current website activity does not establish the end date of its federal award.

entries.name: National Quantum Virtual Laboratory — Quantum Testbeds
entries.focus: Develops distributed quantum testbeds and access to shared capabilities.
entries.materials: Testbeds connect device development, research users and technology translation.
entries.notes: Pilot, design and implementation stages are distinct; the solicitation is not evidence that a complete national laboratory network is already operating.

sources.title: National Quantum Virtual Laboratory — Quantum Testbeds

entries.name: National Quantum and Nanotechnology Infrastructure
entries.focus: Expands access to quantum and nanoscale research facilities.
entries.materials: Shared fabrication and characterization support materials and device research.
entries.notes: The announcement anticipates a network of sites. A completed award roster has not been verified here; this is not a list of established NQNI facilities.

entries.name: Expanding Capacity in Quantum Information Science and Engineering
entries.focus: Builds quantum research and education capacity at a wider range of institutions.
entries.materials: Supports teams and expertise that can participate in quantum materials and device research.
entries.notes: The cited funding cycle is historical; check the NSF page for future opportunities. This entry does not imply an open call.

sources.title: Expanding Capacity in Quantum Information Science and Engineering

entries.name: Connections in Quantum Information Science
entries.focus: Connects quantum information proposals with participating disciplinary programs.
entries.materials: Links chemistry, materials, physics, computing, mathematics and engineering.
entries.notes: A cross-cutting route through participating programs, not one institute or one award.

entries.name: Condensed Matter Physics
entries.focus: Supports fundamental experimental and combined experimental–theoretical condensed matter research.
entries.materials: A continuing disciplinary home for electronic, magnetic and other collective behavior in materials.
entries.notes: Broader than quantum technologies; basic materials research does not depend on an immediate device application.

entries.name: Designing Materials to Revolutionize and Engineer our Future
entries.focus: Connects experiments, computation, theory and data to accelerate materials discovery.
entries.materials: A route for quantum materials design within a broader materials program.
entries.notes: Associated with the Materials Genome Initiative; not a quantum-only program.

sources.title: Designing Materials to Revolutionize and Engineer our Future

entries.name: Materials Innovation Platforms
entries.focus: Combines materials synthesis, characterization and theoretical tools in shared platforms.
entries.materials: Users can develop new electronic and quantum materials through iterative design.
entries.status: Platform network; cited NSF funding solicitation is archived
entries.notes: An archived call is not evidence that the platform network has closed. Consult the platform network for access and current facilities.

entries.name: Quantum foundries / Quantum Accelerators for Materials Science and Engineering
entries.focus: Supports coordinated creation and characterization of materials for quantum technologies.
entries.materials: Makes materials discovery and synthesis part of quantum hardware development.
entries.notes: UCSB Quantum Foundry and MonArk are documented examples. This entry is not a claim of an open funding call or a complete award history.

sources.title: Quantum foundries / Quantum Accelerators for Materials Science and Engineering

entries.name: UCSB Quantum Foundry
entries.focus: Develops materials and interfaces for coherent quantum systems.
entries.materials: Studies entangled states, topological materials and interfaces linking quantum platforms.

entries.name: MonArk Quantum Foundry
entries.lead: Montana State University and University of Arkansas
entries.focus: Develops and characterizes two-dimensional materials for quantum devices.
entries.materials: Links atomically thin materials, magnetism, ferroelectricity and quantum information.
entries.notes: The year marks the September 2021 foundry announcement.

entries.name: National Quantum Information Science Research Centers
entries.focus: Coordinates five national-laboratory-led research consortia.
entries.materials: Materials, quantum devices, software and scientific applications are developed together.
entries.status: All five centers renewed in November 2025
entries.notes: DOE announced a five-year renewal subject to appropriations and award negotiations. The five named centers are all included in this directory.
